paragraphs: Numerical integration estimates an integral from evaluations of a function. Bayesian cubature treats this as inference, producing uncertainty about the integral as well as an estimate. The paper addresses a weakness of that approach: its estimates can be inaccurate and highly sensitive to the prior in high-dimensional domains.

Bayes-Sard cubature combines a Gaussian process model with a parametric regression model for its mean. The regression features are selected test functions, and each coefficient receives an improper prior. This construction guarantees exact integration of those test functions while leaving the nonparametric component flexibility to represent other behavior. It brings a concrete property of classical integration rules into a probabilistic framework.

The authors establish asymptotic convergence and numerically verify their theoretical results. For one high-dimensional financial integral, they report an error reduction of two orders of magnitude relative to Bayesian cubature. That result demonstrates the potential value of combining exactness for chosen functions with uncertainty-aware integration; it is a finding for the reported application rather than a universal improvement factor.
neurips-2018-a-bayes-sard-cubature-metho.tldr: Bayes-Sard cubature combines probabilistic integration with exact integration of selected test functions to improve robustness.

paragraphs: A nearest-neighbor graph connects every data point to its k closest points. Many algorithms construct such graphs, but their settings do not always clearly indicate how accurate the result will be. This paper asks whether a graph can be checked efficiently after construction, without inspecting its entire collection of connections.

The authors formulate this as property testing: distinguish a correct k-nearest-neighbor graph from one requiring changes to more than an epsilon fraction of its edges. Their randomized tester has one-sided error, so a correct graph is not mistakenly rejected. Its inspection complexity is O(sqrt(n) k² / epsilon²), where n is the number of points. They also establish a lower bound of Omega(sqrt(n / (epsilon k))), providing a theoretical constraint on the inspection effort required.

Experiments apply the tester to graphs produced by several algorithms. The tester detects poorly accurate graphs in significantly less time than those graphs took to build. The contribution is therefore an efficient quality check with a precisely defined error criterion, rather than a replacement method for constructing nearest-neighbor graphs.
neurips-2018-a-theory-based-evaluation-o.tldr: A randomized property tester detects substantially incorrect nearest-neighbor graphs while inspecting only part of their structure.

paragraphs: Image matting estimates how much each pixel belongs to a foreground object. Because the image alone does not uniquely determine that separation, matting methods often need a user-provided trimap or strokes. Good guidance can require substantial effort, especially when users do not know which regions most need clarification.

Active Matting learns where and when to request that guidance. A recurrent reinforcement learning method selects a sequence of informative image regions, and a person supplies simple judgments about them. The selection process explicitly considers the relationship between user input and the matting algorithm. Its objective is to obtain a good foreground matte with as little labeling effort as possible.

The experiments report significantly reduced user effort and performance comparable to using dense trimaps. The framework can produce satisfactory results with just ten queried regions in the reported evaluation. The authors also show that learned knowledge about informative regions transfers across different matting algorithms. This suggests that choosing useful questions can improve the interaction itself, rather than requiring users to master each algorithm's input requirements.
neurips-2018-active-matting-f48048fcf8.tldr: Active Matting learns which image regions to ask users about, reducing the effort needed for foreground extraction.

paragraphs: Learning personalized decisions from historical records is difficult because each record reveals only the outcome of the action actually taken. The historical decision policy may also be unknown. This paper studies both estimating how a proposed policy would perform and learning a policy from such observational data.

Existing weighting approaches attempt to make past observations resemble data generated by the proposed policy, but the paper identifies high variance associated with rejecting observations whose actions disagree with it. The proposed method instead chooses weights directly to balance the available finite sample against the target policy. The authors connect this balancing objective to minimizing worst-case or posterior conditional mean squared error.

Policy learning then becomes a two-level optimization over decision policies and data weights. The authors report substantial empirical improvements in both evaluation and learning, and provide consistency guarantees and regret bounds. The central contribution is to optimize the usefulness of the observed sample directly: balance becomes the mechanism for estimating policy outcomes and guiding which policy to choose.
neurips-2018-balanced-policy-evaluation-.tldr: Directly optimizing data-balancing weights improves the evaluation and learning of personalized policies from observational records.

paragraphs: Recurrent neural networks process sequences by repeatedly updating an internal state. This makes the design of the state transition central to how information moves through a sequence. The paper explores complex-valued representations, which have a long history in digital signal processing but are less common in deep learning architectures.

The proposed recurrent cell combines complex-valued, norm-preserving state transitions with a gating mechanism. Norm preservation constrains how a transition changes the size of the state, while gating provides a way to regulate information flow. Bringing these elements together creates a hybrid recurrent design that incorporates both structured transitions and learned control over the evolving representation.

The authors report strong stability and convergence properties for the resulting network. They also find competitive performance on synthetic memory and adding tasks, along with human motion prediction. These evaluations connect the architectural proposal to both controlled sequence tasks and a real-world prediction setting. The stated finding supports complex gated recurrence as a useful design option, without claiming that it dominates every sequence model.
neurips-2018-complex-gated-recurrent-neu.tldr: A recurrent cell combines complex-valued, norm-preserving transitions with gates and achieves competitive sequence-task performance.

paragraphs: An optimization method produces a sequence of candidate models as it runs. A regularized estimation problem instead changes the learning objective to express a preference among possible solutions. This paper studies how these two ways of shaping a learned model connect, making the implicit regularization of optimization more explicit.

The authors show that individual iterates of methods such as gradient descent and mirror descent are close to solutions of appropriately regularized objectives. The connection is pointwise: it concerns corresponding points along the optimization and regularization paths, rather than only their final destinations. This provides a way to interpret intermediate optimization results through related regularized estimation problems.

The relationship matters because theoretical results can move between the two settings. The paper develops one such transfer by using established analysis of regularized estimators to obtain tight excess risk bounds for optimization iterates. Those bounds address prediction quality relative to an optimal reference. The contribution therefore links the trajectory of computation to statistical performance, extending the analysis beyond whether an optimizer eventually reaches a solution.
neurips-2018-connecting-optimization-and.tldr: Optimization iterates closely track appropriately regularized solutions, enabling statistical guarantees to transfer between the two settings.

paragraphs: Optimizing F-measure online is difficult because the metric cannot be separated into independent contributions from individual training examples. It is also nonconvex in the model parameters. The paper addresses the resulting tension between efficient updates and statistical guarantees about F-measure on the underlying population.

The proposed algorithm simultaneously learns class posterior probabilities and an optimal decision threshold. Threshold learning is formulated as minimizing a stochastic strongly convex function, even though its strong convexity parameter is unknown. A new stochastic optimization component performs this work with low memory and computational costs, making the approach suitable for processing examples incrementally.

Under a mild condition on convergence of the estimated posterior probabilities, the threshold learner achieves a rate of approximately O(1/sqrt(n)), up to logarithmic factors, after n examples. The authors prove that it is faster than a predecessor using heuristic threshold updates. Experiments also support its efficiency against existing online F-measure methods. The theoretical rate is conditional on the probability estimates improving appropriately; it is not an unconditional guarantee for arbitrary probability learners.
neurips-2018-faster-online-learning-of-o.tldr: Jointly learning class probabilities and a decision threshold enables efficient online F-measure optimization with a conditional convergence guarantee.

paragraphs: In over-parameterized learning, identifying a global minimum does not fully explain which solution training will select. This paper asks which global minima are accessible to stochastic gradient descent when its learning rate and batch size are fixed. It approaches the question through the stability of the optimization dynamics.

The analysis introduces a property called non-uniformity and considers it together with sharpness. These properties characterize the stability of a global minimum and, through that stability, its accessibility to a particular SGD algorithm. The emphasis is on how a candidate solution interacts with the update process, adding structure to the question of why different training configurations can select different minima.

A central theoretical conclusion is that learning rate and batch size play distinct roles in this selection process. The reported empirical results appear to correlate well with the theory and provide further support for it. That wording matters: the experiments support the proposed stability account, while the abstract does not present them as establishing a universal description of every SGD trajectory.
neurips-2018-how-sgd-selects-the-global-.tldr: A stability analysis uses sharpness and non-uniformity to explain how learning rate and batch size affect SGD's selection of global minima.

paragraphs: Variational inference learns an approximate probability distribution, but a flexible representation alone does not ensure that training finds a useful approximation. The optimization process can restrict which density is ultimately learned. This paper focuses on that gap between what an approximate distribution can represent and what its training procedure actually discovers.

The authors demonstrate drawbacks of biasing the true posterior toward a single mode and introduce Annealed Variational Objectives for hierarchical variational methods. Inspired by Annealed Importance Sampling, the method incorporates energy tempering into the training objective. This changes the optimization problem to facilitate exploration of latent space, addressing the learning process alongside the expressive capacity of the approximation.

Experiments show benefits from encouraging latent-space exploration and report robustness to deterministic warm up. These findings support the idea that the objective used during training can matter even when the distribution family is already expressive. The paper's contribution is therefore an annealed training approach for hierarchical inference, with empirical evidence that improved exploration helps the learned approximation.
neurips-2018-improving-explorability-in-.tldr: Annealed Variational Objectives use energy tempering to encourage latent-space exploration during hierarchical variational inference.

paragraphs: Loop invariants describe properties that remain true as a program loop executes and help establish program correctness. Inferring them is undecidable in general, and practical cases can still be difficult. Code2Inv treats invariant construction as a sequence of decisions informed by a graph-based memory of the program.

The framework learns through reinforcement learning, avoiding the need for known correct invariants as training labels. An automated theorem prover supplies a binary reward only after a complete candidate is proposed. This makes feedback extremely sparse: the learner must discover useful construction strategies despite receiving no such reward for individual intermediate choices.

On 133 benchmark problems, Code2Inv solves 106, compared with 73 for a stochastic search system, 77 for a heuristic search system, and 100 for a decision tree learning system. The learned strategy also transfers to new programs, where a pretrained agent finds solutions more sample efficiently than solving from scratch. These results demonstrate useful learned guidance on the benchmark while leaving the general undecidability of invariant inference intact.
neurips-2018-learning-loop-invariants-fo.tldr: Code2Inv learns to construct loop invariants using program-graph memory and sparse feedback from a theorem prover.

paragraphs: Planning among other agents requires reasoning about actions whose causes may be only partly visible. Interactive partially observable Markov decision processes address this by including models of other agents in the state. Their beliefs form a hierarchy, allowing an agent to reason about what another agent believes and how it chooses actions.

The paper combines Bayesian inference with sequential Monte Carlo sampling to learn intentional models of other agents. Such models attribute beliefs, preferences, and rational action selection to the agents being modeled. The proposed learning procedure covers beliefs and strategy levels, along with transition, observation, and reward functions, giving it a broad role within the interactive planning framework.

Empirical results show accurate learning of another agent's model and better performance than methods using subintentional models. The approach also mitigates the complexity arising from nested beliefs. Its significance is to make richer models of other decision makers more manageable: predicting behavior can draw on inferred intentions while sampling helps handle the computational burden of maintaining hierarchical uncertainty.
neurips-2018-learning-others-intentional.tldr: Bayesian inference and sequential Monte Carlo learn other agents' intentional models within interactive POMDPs.

paragraphs: This paper converts simple hand-drawn images into graphics programs written in a subset of LaTeX. The goal is to recover a structured description of how to draw the image. Such a description can express relationships and repeated operations that are less explicit in a collection of image pixels.

The model combines two learned stages. A convolutional neural network first proposes plausible drawing primitives that explain the image. Those primitives become a specification of what the graphics program should produce. A second model uses program synthesis techniques to recover a program from that specification, connecting visual recognition to the search for executable structure.

The recovered programs can contain variable bindings, loops, and simple conditional constructs. Having this program representation allows the system to correct errors made by the visual network and extrapolate drawings. The contribution is the connection between recognizing graphical elements and recovering a program that organizes them. Its stated scope is simple drawings and a restricted graphics language, where the inferred structure supports operations beyond reproducing the observed image.
neurips-2018-learning-to-infer-graphics-.tldr: A neural recognition model and program synthesis recover structured graphics programs from simple hand drawings.

paragraphs: Domain generalization asks whether a model trained on available domains can work well in new domains at test time. Success within a training domain does not directly establish this ability. MetaReg addresses the problem by making cross-domain performance the target of a learned regularization function.

The method places the search for that regularizer inside a meta-learning framework. It learns a regularizer that encourages a model trained on one domain to perform well on another. This connects the training preference imposed by regularization to the particular behavior sought at deployment: carrying useful knowledge across changes in domain. The regularizer itself is therefore an object of learning.

Experiments on computer vision and natural language datasets indicate that the method can learn regularizers with good cross-domain generalization. The evidence supports the proposed way of encoding transfer into training, rather than guaranteeing success on every unseen domain. The paper's main contribution is a concrete learning-to-learn formulation in which performance across domains determines what kind of regularization should guide the underlying model.
neurips-2018-metareg-towards-domain-gene.tldr: MetaReg learns a regularizer by training it to promote good performance across different domains.

paragraphs: Sampling from a distribution becomes harder when valid samples must obey constraints. This paper develops a unified framework inspired by mirror descent for deriving first-order sampling algorithms. It addresses both algorithm design and non-asymptotic analysis, which describes convergence at a finite computational budget.

For a general target distribution with a strongly convex potential, the framework implies the existence of an algorithm with approximately O(epsilon⁻² d) convergence complexity, suppressing logarithmic factors. This suggests a substantial improvement over the cited O(epsilon⁻⁶ d⁵) rate. The strong convexity assumption is central to that stated result, and the abstract frames the general result as an existence implication of the framework.

The authors also specialize the approach to Dirichlet posteriors, motivated by Latent Dirichlet Allocation. They derive a first-order non-asymptotic rate of approximately O(epsilon⁻² d²), extend the framework to mini-batches with stochastic gradients, and prove convergence rates there. Promising LDA experiments on real datasets complement the analysis. Together, these contributions connect a general constrained-sampling framework to a specific probabilistic modeling application.
neurips-2018-mirrored-langevin-dynamics-.tldr: A mirror-descent-inspired framework yields constrained sampling algorithms with improved theoretical rates under stated assumptions.

paragraphs: Electromagnetic brain activity is often studied through frequency-specific oscillations, but some neural waveforms may have more complex shapes than sinusoids. The paper proposes learning representations directly from recordings so that analysis can capture temporal structure beyond the patterns emphasized by traditional frequency-based representations.

Its multivariate convolutional sparse coding method learns both prototypical temporal waveforms and their associated spatial patterns across EEG or MEG measurements. Linking these two components makes it possible to characterize a waveform and localize its origin in the brain. The optimization alternates between components and uses a greedy coordinate descent solver, with reported state-of-the-art running time on long time series.

Applied to MEG data, the method recovers biological artifacts and reveals non-sinusoidal mu-shaped patterns with topographic maps related to the somatosensory cortex. These findings show why learning waveform shape and spatial organization together can matter. The representation exposes structure that is relevant to interpreting the recording, while the efficient solver supports applying the approach to long sequences of measurements.
neurips-2018-multivariate-convolutional-.tldr: Multivariate convolutional sparse coding learns brain-signal waveforms and spatial patterns, revealing non-sinusoidal structure in MEG recordings.

paragraphs: Programming by example asks a system to construct a program that matches supplied input-output pairs. The challenge is searching through possible programs efficiently. This paper combines a neural model with miniKanren, a constraint logic programming system, so that learned guidance can influence the symbolic search.

The neural model receives miniKanren's internal representation of the problem. That representation expresses the examples as recursive constraints, giving the learner access to the structure used by the search system itself. The authors explore recurrent and graph neural networks for this role and contribute a modified version of miniKanren that an external agent can drive.

The reported results show faster synthesis in many cases and generalization to larger problems. These are qualified findings, rather than a claim of faster search for every task. The key contribution is the interface between learning and logic: a neural model guides decisions using the search engine's constraints, allowing information from the symbolic reasoning process to inform how the system searches for a matching program.
neurips-2018-neural-guided-constraint-lo.tldr: Neural models guide miniKanren using its internal constraints, speeding program synthesis in many cases and generalizing to larger problems.

paragraphs: Hybrid stochastic gradient descent combines features of stochastic and full-gradient methods for objectives expressed as finite sums. Earlier convergence analysis covered convex problems with sampling that allows replacement. This paper asks whether the method's advantages can extend to sampling without replacement and to nonconvex objectives.

The authors show that, in both convex and nonconvex settings under without-replacement sampling, constant-step-size HSGD can match full gradient descent's convergence rate while retaining incremental first-order oracle complexity comparable to stochastic gradient descent and independent of sample size. These are two distinct advantages: how quickly convergence progresses and how much incremental gradient information is required.

For a special class of finite-sum objectives using linear prediction models, some convergence results can be improved further. Numerical experiments support the theoretical findings and demonstrate favorable efficiency for the without-replacement version. The contribution broadens the settings in which HSGD's combined advantages can be established, while retaining the qualified claim that the stronger linear-model results apply only in some cases.
neurips-2018-new-insight-into-hybrid-sto.tldr: Hybrid SGD can retain favorable convergence and oracle complexity under without-replacement sampling, including for nonconvex problems.

paragraphs: Sum-product networks combine characteristics of deep neural networks and probabilistic graphical models. Their appeal includes clear probabilistic meaning and tractable inference. These benefits depend on structural requirements called completeness and decomposability, so choosing the network's connections is part of ensuring that the representation works as intended.

Because constructing a valid architecture by hand is difficult, structure learning is commonly used. This paper introduces an online structure learning technique for both feed-forward and recurrent sum-product networks. It addresses the architecture itself, extending the learning problem beyond selecting numerical parameters for a network whose organization has already been fixed.

The authors demonstrate the algorithm on real-world datasets with continuous features, including sequences of different lengths. These settings are ones where the appropriate architecture is not obvious in advance. The stated contribution is a method for learning structure across both ordinary and recurrent SPNs, illustrated on practical data. The abstract reports those demonstrations without asserting a particular accuracy improvement or a universal advantage over other structure learning methods.
neurips-2018-online-structure-learning-f.tldr: An online algorithm learns the structure of feed-forward and recurrent sum-product networks, including for variable-length sequence data.

paragraphs: Visual question answering systems can exploit correlations between question wording and answers while paying too little attention to the image. Standard evaluation may conceal this behavior when similar language biases occur in both training and test data. The paper develops a training procedure to reduce this reliance on linguistic shortcuts.

A question-only adversary receives the VQA model's question encoding and tries to predict answers from it. Adversarial training discourages the VQA model from encoding language biases that help this adversary succeed. The method also uses the question-only model to estimate the mutual information between image and answer given the question, then explicitly maximizes that quantity to encourage visual grounding.

The procedure is model agnostic and improves multiple base models on a bias-sensitive VQA split, reaching the reported state of the art there. On standard VQA tasks, it incurs significantly less accuracy loss than existing bias-reduction methods. These findings indicate that training can encourage stronger use of image content while preserving more standard-task performance than the compared approaches.
neurips-2018-overcoming-language-priors-.tldr: A question-only adversary and an information-based objective encourage VQA models to ground answers more strongly in images.

paragraphs: Compositional data contains nonnegative parts that sum to a fixed total. This constraint makes the parts statistically dependent, complicating the direct use of standard analysis tools. The paper studies how to learn a low-dimensional representation while accounting for that structure, with principal component analysis as its starting point.

The proposed approach combines benefits of log-ratio transformations with exponential family PCA, allowing representation learning directly from the original data. Its derivation generalizes the scaled Bregman theorem, relating transformed divergences through an additional remainder term. This mathematical connection supports a surrogate loss that upper-bounds the exponential family PCA loss and has a form that is easier to optimize.

The authors also derive a corresponding formulation for nonlinear autoencoders, extending the approach beyond linear representations. Experiments on simulated and microbiome data show promise. The contribution brings the dependence inherent in fixed-total data into the representation-learning objective, and supplies a practical optimization surrogate. The stated empirical evidence supports the approach's potential without claiming superiority for every kind of compositional dataset.
neurips-2018-representation-learning-of-.tldr: A compositional-data objective combines log-ratio ideas with exponential family PCA and extends to nonlinear autoencoders.

paragraphs: Accidents are rare, which makes estimating autonomous-driving risk through ordinary driving extremely expensive. The paper argues that statistical validation through real-world testing would require billions of miles and expose the public to danger. It develops a simulation framework that evaluates an entire driving system, including deep-learning perception and control.

The framework uses adaptive importance sampling to accelerate the estimation of rare-event probabilities. It focuses simulation effort on informative events while estimating accident probability under a base distribution representing standard traffic behavior. The target remains risk under that specified traffic distribution, making the probability model an explicit part of what the evaluation measures.

In a highway scenario, the authors report evaluation speedups of 2–20 times over naive Monte Carlo sampling. They also report 10–300P times acceleration over real-world testing, where P is the number of processors. These results demonstrate faster evaluation in the studied scenario. The contribution combines full-system simulation with targeted rare-event estimation, addressing the difficulty of observing enough accidents to estimate their probability efficiently.
neurips-2018-scalable-end-to-end-autonom.tldr: Adaptive importance sampling accelerates full-system autonomous-driving simulation for estimating rare accident probabilities.

paragraphs: Few-shot learning asks a model to generalize from only a small number of examples. TADAM studies how the metric used to compare examples affects this process. The paper identifies two influential choices: the scale of the metric and whether the comparison space adapts to the current task's sample set.

The analysis shows that simple metric scaling can fundamentally change parameter updates. For certain metrics on mini-ImageNet's five-way, five-shot classification task, scaling improves accuracy by up to 14%. The authors then condition the learner on the task examples so that it learns a task-dependent metric space, and introduce an end-to-end training procedure using auxiliary task co-training.

The resulting model combines metric scaling with task adaptation and achieves the reported state of the art on mini-ImageNet. The authors also confirm their findings on a few-shot dataset they introduce using CIFAR100. The significance is that both numerical scaling and task context affect how comparisons are learned; a distance function's role extends beyond simply ranking examples after training.
neurips-2018-tadam-task-dependent-adapti.tldr: TADAM improves few-shot learning by scaling comparison metrics and adapting the metric space to each task's examples.

paragraphs: This paper presents a text-to-speech system that can generate speech in voices absent from its training data. It transfers information learned through speaker verification into speech synthesis, using seconds of reference speech to specify the target voice. The system separates speaker representation, speech generation, and waveform generation into independently trained components.

A speaker encoder learns from noisy, untranscribed speech from thousands of speakers and produces a fixed-dimensional voice embedding. A Tacotron 2-based synthesis network uses the text and embedding to generate a mel spectrogram. An autoregressive WaveNet-based vocoder then converts that representation into waveform samples. This arrangement lets speaker knowledge learned from an independent dataset condition the synthesis process.

The authors demonstrate natural-sounding synthesis for previously unseen speakers and quantify the importance of training the encoder on a large, diverse speaker collection. They also generate novel voices from randomly sampled embeddings, with voices dissimilar to those in training. These findings support the usefulness of the learned speaker representation both for transferring a reference voice and for generating new voice characteristics.
neurips-2018-transfer-learning-from-spea.tldr: Speaker-verification embeddings condition a text-to-speech system that generates natural speech in previously unseen voices.

paragraphs: Optimization on a manifold concerns variables whose possible values have geometric structure. This paper develops a variational approach to accelerated optimization in that setting, extending an existing finite-dimensional formulation to infinite-dimensional manifolds. Its motivating example is the space of diffeomorphisms, used in computer-vision registration problems.

The authors derive partial differential equations describing the continuous evolution of the optimization process and relate them to mechanical principles. Their formulation evolves infinitely many particles represented by a mass density. That density changes alongside the optimization variable and contributes to the particles' dynamics, making the evolving distribution of mass part of the acceleration mechanism.

The approach can also be interpreted as a generalization of the L² optimal mass transport problem. The paper develops the theory, computes the acceleration equations, and illustrates the behavior of the resulting scheme. Its contribution is a formulation of accelerated dynamics for an infinite-dimensional geometric setting. The stated results concern the derivation and illustrated behavior of those dynamics, rather than a quantified performance advantage on registration benchmarks.
neurips-2018-variational-pdes-for-accele.tldr: A variational framework derives accelerated optimization PDEs on infinite-dimensional manifolds using evolving mass-density dynamics.

paragraphs: Retracing a demonstrated path becomes difficult when actions are noisy or the environment changes. The paper studies how a learned system can follow a route both forwards and backwards under those conditions. Its approach uses a visual abstraction of the demonstration to support decisions during the later traversal.

Two networks divide the task. The first converts the demonstrated path into an abstract representation. The second combines that representation with its observations of the world to decide how to act. Both networks are optimized together end to end, so the path representation is learned in connection with the needs of the network that must use it.

The authors evaluate forward and backward path following in two realistic simulators. Their approach outperforms a classical method and several other baselines in these experiments. The results support the usefulness of jointly learning a path memory and an action policy for retracing routes under uncertainty. The reported evidence comes from simulated environments, where noisy actuation and environmental changes are part of the task being addressed.
neurips-2018-visual-memory-for-robust-pa.tldr: Two jointly trained networks learn a visual path memory and use it to retrace routes forwards and backwards under uncertainty.
